name: How big should my shower niche be for shampoo, soap, and family-size bottles?

mainEntity.name: How big should my shower niche be for shampoo, soap, and family-size bottles?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A niche does not have one universal correct size; it should fit the household’s products, the wall framing, and the tile pattern. Elite Remodeling & Design can use the selected tile and intended bottle sizes to develop finished dimensions before framing begins.

Key factors:
- Measure tall bottles, pump clearance, and refill containers.
- Allow room for tile, mortar, trim, and grout joints.
- Decide whether one large compartment or separate shelves will be easier to use.

Practical guidance: Place the products you actually use on a counter and measure their width, height, and depth. Add practical clearance rather than designing only to a nominal product size. A wider niche may improve storage but can require more framing, trim, waterproofing, and tile planning.

Elite Remodeling & Design can show the proposed niche proportions during design development so the storage plan supports the rest of the bathroom.
acceptedAnswer.description: Size the niche around your actual products, tile dimensions, wall depth, and shelf plan. Measure tall bottles and pump clearance, then account for tile, mortar, trim, and grout. A design drawing helps confirm the usable finished opening before framing.
